ETF flows tell a story: institutional money moving under the radar while retail shakes out.

The Cantillon effect works both ways — those close to the traditional financial apparatus get the advantage. Wall Street gets the new money first, through ETFs and QE, before prices adjust. Main Street gets inflation, volatility, and exit liquidity.

Bitcoin levels this playing field.

There's no "first-mover advantage" from a printer. No one gets Bitcoin because they work at BlackRock. The rules are the same for everyone: proof-of-work, digital scarcity, voluntary exchange.

That's why they want to regulate it, censor it, "manage" it. They're trying to recreate Cantillon advantages in Bitcoin.

But they can't. The protocol doesn't care who you are. Only that you follow the rules.

That's honest money.
